transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03
Start: 10:30 AM UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Evan Brooks, Maura Chen (Redwood); Lydia Park, Samir Patel, Carlos Mejia, Nora Black, Jaya Iyer (MediQuantix)

Summary: quick deep dive on week-2 bench results vs customer incumbent; focus on p95 latency delta, sustained throughput, routing failover play, and security/ procurement asks. Agreement to run full 24h ramp and share logs; several action items assigned.

Topics: results recap; quantization and batching tradeoffs; KV/prefix cache impact; routing & fallback to variants; dedicated slot sizing; security questions (KMS, audit); procurement timeline.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Evan Brooks: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, uh we'll run through the bench readout, maura and I will talk numbers then take questions. Lydia, Samir, you good?
[00:15] Lydia Park: yeah all good, thanks. quick note we have Nora from procurement on in case we need to sync on PO stuff.
[00:30] Maura Chen: cool. so quick context, this is the week-2 pilot bench — we compared Redwood dedicated pilot to the customer incumbent which you saw in the spreadsheet. tests were run with your anonymized traces, 4k token average length, mixed chat/generation profile.
[00:48] Samir Patel: just to clarify the incumbent runs were from your existing prod traces or the synthetic ones we gave?
[00:55] Maura Chen: these are your traces flattened — the same seed we used last week, we did a replay in a controlled lab env so it's apples-to-apples. there may be small variance for tail sampling but overall it's consistent.
[01:10] Carlos Mejia: quick Q — did you enable the KV cache on the Redwood run? last time we saw big wins when prefix reuse is high.
[01:18] Maura Chen: yes we ran two profiles. run A had KV/prefix cache enabled and run B disabled to show delta. I'll call out both numbers.
[01:28] Maura Chen: numbers: median latency (per request) for Redwood dedicated was 78 ms, p95 128 ms with cache on. Without cache p95 moves to ~210 ms. Incumbent p95 we observed at ~235 ms in your baseline. So delta p95 vs incumbent is roughly -107 ms in the cache-on case.
[01:50] Samir Patel: those numbers sound good. what's token throughput— like sustained rps?
[01:55] Maura Chen: sustained throughput with batcher tuned was about 145 requests/sec on the pilot slot (single 8xGPU pool equivalent), our observed baseline incumbent sustained at ~94 rps for same payload mix. Peak bursts hit 220 rps for short 20s windows when we allowed higher batching.
[02:15] Lydia Park: so throughput is clearly higher — what's the CPU/GPU utilization and any memory pressure observed?
[02:22] Maura Chen: GPU utilization averaged 62% in steady state, with KV cache increasing memory footprint by about 8GB per worker for the cached keys; CPU for the preproc workers stayed around 28%. no OOMs in our runs. there was a small jitter at p99 during the larger burst windows.
[02:40] Evan Brooks: one point on the jitter — that's why we recommend our routing fallback. if a slot gets overwhelmed we can route to a compatible variant (quantized variant with slightly higher latency but lower cost) automatically. helps keep SLOs rather than erroring out.
[02:55] Carlos Mejia: what compatibility means— will it change output? we can't have hallucination differences between variants.
[03:02] Maura Chen: good question. the compatible variants are tested for semantic parity for your prompts; we do an A/B sample check in the background and keep rollback thresholds. there is a small delta in sampling probability sometimes but we've found for retrieval/assist workloads it's within your tolerance. we'll share the parity report.
[03:20] Samir Patel: can you run one of those parity checks on our five canonical prompts? we want to see exact delta.
[03:26] Maura Chen: yes we'll do that as part of the 24h run.
[03:30] Jaya Iyer: network wise — how are you doing egress and VPC peering? we have strict egress limits and need to ensure private connectivity.
[03:37] Evan Brooks: for the private pilot we used VPC peering and a private control plane option; all egress remains in the peered VPC and we can do customer-managed NAT if you prefer. KMS integration is supported — you bring your key or use our HSM-backed option.
[03:55] Nora Black: and audit logs? SOC2? we need to attach to vendor review pack.
[04:00] Evan Brooks: absolutely — we'll send the security pack, SOC2 Type II reports, ISO docs, and a KMS integration guide. also we provide token-level audit logs and per-request metadata for the entire pilot.
[04:12] Lydia Park: thanks. on the vendor comparison — cost per 1M tokens how does that look for the pilot? rough numbers fine.
[04:18] Evan Brooks: rough ballpark for the pilot config with dedicated slots and caching it's about 35% lower unit cost vs incumbent at your current utilization; we'll produce an exact cost model in the pricing doc Evan: (laugh) sorry, I mean we'll produce the exact numbers by Monday.
[04:34] Samir Patel: what's the effect of aggressive quantization? we ran 4-bit quant in-house and saw quality regressions.
[04:40] Maura Chen: we tested multiple quant profiles. 8-bit mixed quant (Q8/INT8 paths) preserved output quality in our evals; 4-bit (Q4) sometimes introduced tokenization edge blips on named entities. for your prompts — recall is sensitive on drug names — we won't recommend Q4 unless we do targeted evals; instead we suggest hybrid: Q8 for core, Q4 for cold path.
[05:05] Carlos Mejia: can Redwood run the model in the same region to get lower latency — our users are EU based mostly?
[05:11] Maura Chen: yes region pinning is supported. for the pilot we ran in eu-west1; we can also provision dedicated capacity in region of choice.
[05:20] Samir Patel: any differences in how you handle KV cache persistence across restarts? we've hit cold start penalties before.
[05:26] Maura Chen: KV cache is persisted in-memory with warmup prefetch for known prefixes; across full worker replacement we have a fast-warmup path that preloads most frequent prefixes from a small shared cache. that reduces cold-start p95 by ~40% in our tests.
[05:42] Lydia Park: is there a way to simulate our daily diurnal pattern? we need to ensure p95 holds over our peak at 3pm local.
[05:50] Maura Chen: yes the 24h ramp will replay a day of traffic including diurnal spikes and long-tail sessions; we'll include p50/p95/p99 curves across that window.
[06:00] Evan Brooks: quick FYI we saw a case study similar to yours — when prefix reuse is high they saw 2-3x lower per token cost with cache-on. we'll include that in the readout.
[06:12] Samir Patel: good. any behavioral differences during fallback routing — like do you re-run the prompt or chop tokens?
[06:18] Maura Chen: routing is at request boundary; we don't chop tokens. we select the variant that best matches model spec; some variants have slightly different sampling temperature defaults but we respect your specified params.
[06:30] Nora Black: procurement question — what's the minimum commit for dedicated pilot?
[06:35] Evan Brooks: typically a 3-month pilot with a committed minimum for a set number of slots; we'll show flexible burst terms. Evan: pricing will show two flavors — reserved commit and flexible pay-as-you-go breakout.
[06:50] Lydia Park: okay this is helpful. can you also include error budget accounting in the slides? we need to see what happens when you cross SLOs.
[06:58] Maura Chen: yes we'll add an error-budget model and example routing policies — e.g., canary -> canary fallback -> degrade to quantized variant -> route to incumbent as last resort.
[07:15] Samir Patel: curious on telemetry — how granular are logs? we want request token-level timings and GPU op breakdown.
[07:22] Maura Chen: we capture per-request timings (tokenization, model time, postproc), batch sizes, and kernel-level metrics (when enabled). GPU op breakdown is available in the console as time series.
[07:35] Carlos Mejia: will you share the raw bench CSV? we want to run our own analysis.
[07:39] Maura Chen: yes, raw CSVs and the runner configs will be shared.
[07:45] Evan Brooks: okay wrapping — I'll summarize next steps.
[07:50] Evan Brooks: action items: Redwood to send security package, pricing, routing playbook; Maura to run the 24h ramp including cache-on/off and parity checks on your five prompts; Samir to provide the canonical prompts and SLOs; Carlos to confirm peering window; Nora to share procurement timeline.
[08:08] Nora Black: noted, timeline looks feasible, will try to get procurement items by Aug 12.
[08:13] Lydia Park: thanks — we'll reconvene after the ramp, please include an executive slide for the Aug 16 readout.
[08:20] Evan Brooks: will do. any final q's?
[08:23] Samir Patel: only one — can we request a run with disabled batching so we can see pure latency per-token?
[08:29] Maura Chen: yes, we'll include a low-batch/no-batch run in the 24h to show pure latency baseline.
[08:35] Jaya Iyer: one more — can you annotate runs with exact kernel selection (cuBLAS vs custom kernels) cause our infra folks like that detail.
[08:42] Maura Chen: yes we'll expose kernel selections and compilation flags in the runner metadata.
[08:48] Evan Brooks: perfect, thanks all. we'll follow up with artifacts by the dates noted.
[08:55] Meeting end.
